resources.string: SMSGate sends your messages from this phone. Allow these so it works reliably, even with the screen off.
SMSGate can’t send messages until you allow SMS. You can do it later from this screen.
Lets SMSGate send the messages your apps queue, as normal texts from this phone’s SIM.
Lists your SIMs so messages can go out from the one you choose. Your number is shared only if Android provides it.
Shows a quiet notice while SMSGate stays connected, and tells you if sending stops.
Stops Android from pausing SMSGate, so messages go out on time while the phone sleeps.
If Android doesn’t ask again, turn it on in the app’s settings.
Turn on Autostart for SMSGate, then set its Battery saver to No restrictions (Settings › Apps › SMSGate). Locking SMSGate in recent apps also helps.
Open Settings › Battery › Background usage limits and add SMSGate to Never sleeping apps. Make sure it isn’t in Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps.
Open Settings › Battery › App launch, turn off Manage automatically for SMSGate, and allow Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
Allow Auto launch for SMSGate, then set its battery usage to Allow background activity (Settings › Apps › SMSGate › Battery).
Open Settings › Battery › Battery optimisation, choose SMSGate and select Don’t optimise. Allow Auto launch too if your phone offers it.
Allow Autostart for SMSGate in i Manager, and set its Background power consumption to Allow (Settings › Battery).
Link it to your SMSGate account. On the dashboard, open Devices and choose Pair a phone.
Point the camera at the code on the dashboard.
Type the 8-character code shown under the QR code.
Use your account email and password.

Google Play services isn’t available on this phone, so QR scanning is off: enter the pairing code instead. New messages then arrive through a sync every 15 minutes, or instantly with Always connected turned on.
This phone’s name, SIM details and push token will be sent to this server. Continue only if it’s the address of your SMSGate dashboard.
Enter a valid HTTPS address, e.g. https://sms.example.com.
Enter all 8 characters of the code.
Names must be between 1 and 64 characters.
That code is invalid or has expired. Generate a new one on the dashboard and try again.
That email or password doesn’t look right.
Verify your email address first. Check your inbox for the link.
Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.

On battery, Android pauses background network use. Allow SMSGate to run in the background so Always connected keeps working. Otherwise messages still arrive by push or the 15-minute sync, just not always instantly.
It’s removed from your account, stops sending, and any message it picked up but hasn’t sent is marked failed. Its message log stays on the phone.
